verdict.rationale: Omarchy is a desktop Linux distribution, so running on single-board computers is a fair axis, but the evidence pack never mentions single-board computers or ARM boards. The nearest evidence is a claim that a 2011 ThinkPad with 2GB RAM can run it and a community install on a €30 x86 Chromebook, where the ISO route failed. Both are low-cost conventional machines, not single-board computers, so they are adjacent and earn no credit.

support.subject: As a developer, I can get a full desktop developer experience running on low-cost single-board computers
